_comment: Configuration for the integration test host (IntegrationTestFactory uses
UseEnvironment("Testing")).
Both values below are read eagerly, while Program.cs is still composing the
builder: it reads Auth:Mode before AddInnovayseAuth, and hands the configuration
to AddInfrastructure, which reads EncryptionKey. WebApplicationFactory merges its
own sources in afterwards, so a value supplied through ConfigureAppConfiguration
arrives too late to be seen, and that is what made all 41 tests report "the entry
point exited without ever building an IHost". appsettings.{Environment}.json is
part of WebApplicationBuilder's own defaults, which is early enough.
Auth:Mode is local because every test here creates its users through
POST /api/auth/register, and LocalAuthController 404s that action in any other
mode. The connection string is deliberately absent: Testcontainers assigns a
random port, so the factory supplies it at runtime, and that one works through the
in-memory source because AddDbContext reads configuration inside a deferred
lambda.
The key is a throwaway. It encrypts nothing that outlives the test container,
and it is a real key rather than an exemption so the tests exercise the same
encrypting EF converters production uses.
Smtp:Encryption is here because AddInfrastructure validates it on start and the
base appsettings.json deliberately carries no value for it -- an absent key is a
refusal to boot, which is the point of it, and would otherwise take every test in
this suite down with the host. 'none' is what a test host that sends no mail at
all should say: stated, like every other tier has to state it.
//Cors: The gateway return-URL check refuses any origin not listed here, so the payment tests need
one. It used to arrive from appsettings.json, which now holds no per-tier values at all --
every deployment supplies its own through Cors__AllowedOrigins__N.
//ScheduledJobs: The integration tests dispatch the same job over and over against one database. A job that rests
after a success would refuse the second run, so the rest is off here.
//SshAgent: The address HostPanel's agent connections come from, which the server SSH setup screen shows
in its firewall and sshd lines; the server SSH setup tests assert both families.
